content: The text provided is a list of references formatted in a bibliographic style, detailing various studies and publications related to nutrition, supplementation, and health interventions. 1. Ekbote VH, Khadilkar AV, Chiplonkar SA, Hanumante NM, Khadilkar VV, Mughal MZ conducted a pilot randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effects of oral calcium and vitamin D supplementation using fortified laddoos in underprivileged Indian toddlers. (Eur J Clin Nutr. 2011;65(4):440-6). 2. Emel K, Ziauddin H, Melody CT, Shabina R, Noor Ahmad K, Stanley HZ explored the use of home fortification with Sprinkles™ to reduce childhood anemia, sharing lessons learned from the North West Frontier Province in Pakistan. (2006; p. 35-40). 3. Ernst J, Ettyang G, Neumann C investigated the use of high-nutrition biscuits as a dietary supplement to increase animal protein intake among HIV-infected Kenyan women and their children. (Annals of Nutrition and Metabolism. 2013;63:144). 4. Ernst J, Ettyang G, Neumann CG conducted a study in progress on high-nutrition biscuits to enhance animal protein intake in the diets of HIV-infected Kenyan women and their children. (Food Nutr Bull. 2014;35(4 Suppl):S198-204). 5. Faber M analyzed the complementary foods consumed by 6-12-month-old rural infants in South Africa, finding them inadequate in micronutrients. (Public Health Nutrition. 2005;8(4):373-81). 6. Fatmah developed MOCAF TEMPEH DATE biscuits aimed at improving the nutritional status of underweight children. (Int J Geomate. 2018;15(49):155-61). 7. Ferreira HdS, Cavalcante SdA, Cabral Júnior CR, Paffer ATd studied the effects of consuming a multimistura on the nutritional status of children living in a favela on the outskirts of Maceió, Alagoas, Brazil. (Rev bras saúde matern infant. 2008;8(3):309-18). 8. FHI, International Food Policy Research Institute, and Project Concern International evaluated the integration of maternal, infant, and young child nutrition (MIYCN) interventions into existing programs. (2018). 9. Filteau S, Baisley K, Chisenga M, Kasonka L, Gibson RS conducted a randomized controlled trial to assess whether micronutrient-fortified food provided from 6 months of age could enable HIV-exposed, uninfected Zambian children to catch up in growth compared to HIV-unexposed children. (Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes. 2011;56(2):166-75). 10. Fink G, Levenson R, Tembo S, Rockers PC evaluated the impact of homeand community-based growth monitoring on reducing early-life growth faltering through an open-label, cluster-randomized controlled trial. (Am J Clin Nutr. 2017;106(4):1070-7). 11. Finn K, Callen C, Bhatia J, Reidy K, Bechard LJ, Carvalho R emphasized the importance of dietary sources of iron in infants and toddlers, drawing lessons from the FITS study. (Nutrients. 2017;9(7):9). 12. Fleige LE, Sahyoun NR, Murphy SP developed a new simulation model to estimate micronutrient levels for inclusion in fortified blended foods used in food aid programs. (J Nutr. 2010;140(2):355-65). 13. Food U, Nutrition S, Westat, University of California LA, University of California B conducted the Feeding My Baby national WIC study. (2018). 14. Friel JK, Qasem W, Cai C, Hossain Z, Jorgensen S, Zackert B, et al. examined the role of iron and complementary feeding in breastfed infants. (Free Radical Biology & Medicine. 2013;65:S108-S9). 15. Friel J, Azad E, Azad M, Qasem W, Cai C, Kafipour E investigated the impact of iron-rich foods on gut inflammation and microbiota in breastfed infants. (FASEB Journal. 2015;29(1 Meeting Abstracts)). 16. Fuchs GJ, De Wier M, Hutchinson SW, Farris RP, Doucet H, Schwartz S, et al. studied the impact of whole cow's milk with iron-fortified cereal or formula on dietary intake and iron status in infants aged 6-12 months. (Am J Clin Nutr. 1991;53(5):P-18). 17. Gannon B, Kaliwile C, Arscott S, Schmaelzle S, Masi C, Chileshe J, et al. demonstrated that biofortified orange maize is as efficacious as a vitamin A supplement in Zambian children, even in the presence of high liver reserves of vitamin A. (FASEB Journal. 2014;28(1 SUPPL. 1)). 18. García-Guerra A, Rivera-Dommarco J, Neufeld L, Domínguez-Islas CP evaluated the effect of three supplements with equal micronutrient content on serum zinc concentrations in Mexican children. (FASEB Journal. 2009;23(S1)). 19. Geltman PL, Hironaka LK, Mehta SD, Padilla P, Rodrigues P, Meyers AF, et al. conducted a randomized clinical trial comparing adherence to iron supplementation using ferrous fumarate sprinkles versus ferrous sulfate drops in low-income infants. (J Pediatr. 2009;154(5):738-43). 20. Ghosh S, Strutt N, Otoo GE, Suri DJ, Ankrah J, Johnson T, et al. assessed the provision of a macroand micronutrient-fortified complementary food supplement on the nutritional status of Ghanaian infants. (FASEB Journal. 2017;31(1)). 21. Gough EK, Moulton LH, Mutasa K, Ntozini R, Stoltzfus RJ, Majo FD, et al. investigated the effects of improved water, sanitation, hygiene, and complementary feeding on environmental enteric dysfunction in children in rural Zimbabwe through a cluster-randomized controlled trial. (PLoS Negl Trop Dis. 2020;14(2):e0007963). 22. Grantham-McGregor S, Powell C, Walker S reviewed the relationship between nutritional supplements, stunting, and child development. (Lancet. 1989;2(8666):809-10). 23. Gunaratna NS, Bosha T, Belayneh D, Fekadu T, De Groote H studied the acceptance of biofortified quality protein maize for complementary feeding among women and children in rural Ethiopia. (J Sci Food Agric. 2016;96(10):3439-45). 24. Hambidge KM, Chavez MN, Brown RM, Walravens PA evaluated the zinc nutritional status of young middle-income children and the effects of consuming zinc-fortified breakfast cereals. (Am J Clin Nutr. 1979;32(12):2532-9). 25. Hoffman DR, Theuer RC, Castaneda YS, Wheaton DH, Bosworth RG, O'Connor AR, et al. found that the maturation of visual acuity is accelerated in breastfed term infants fed baby food containing DHA-enriched egg yolk. (J Nutr. 2004;134(9):2307-13).
